whoop: In a cleared room with a guarded whoop, fly a slow lap around two floor markers as if delivering very fragile soup.
Mark a broad parking bay on the floor. Approach from two different directions and land fully inside it.
Fly a square around four widely spaced floor markers. Make the corners gentle and stop before drifting beyond the course.
Hold a steady heading while moving slowly sideways between two markers. Your imaginary passengers dislike yaw.
Fly one slow clockwise lap, land, then repeat anticlockwise. Compare which direction felt less coordinated.
In a safe clear space, practise three gentle descents to a large pad without bouncing. The landing inspector is a fictional potato.
Place two large pads apart in an empty room. Shuttle between them twice, landing and pausing on each.
Use a wide, soft, freestanding gate in a clear area. Make three slow centred passes; land if the line feels cramped.
Film a tiny nature documentary about an empty cardboard box from a generous distance. Keep the camera motion calm.
Fly towards a floor marker, stop short, then turn away smoothly. Treat it as an invisible customer-service desk.
Choose two existing rate profiles in the simulator. Fly the same easy route and note which produces fewer corrections.
Make one continuous slow shot linking three widely separated floor markers. Imagine each is a different planetary embassy.
Practise an unhurried takeoff, brief steady hover and controlled landing as one clean sequence. Repeat only while the pack remains healthy.
Fly a broad oval with the same visible ground clearance on both long sides. Review the recording for height changes.
At a safe clear site, fly a smooth diagonal across a large marked rectangle. Align with the destination before descending.
In the simulator, complete an easy course without touching the gates. Smoothness earns the imaginary award, speed earns nothing.
Use a guarded whoop in a cleared room to film a slow reveal from beside a large box, with ample separation.
Fly a short straight line at walking pace, land, then repeat it more smoothly. Compare the two clips side by side.
Put a large paper H on the floor. Make one careful approach with the H upright in the view, then one from the side.
Plan a tiny rescue route between three floor pads. Visit each in order and return before the normal battery warning; rescue nobody real.
camera: Film a stationary empty scene twice: once with a slow rise, once with a slow lateral slide. Compare the sense of scale.
At an authorised open site, frame a distant landmark and make a gentle sideward move that reveals background parallax.
Record a ten-second static composition with a level horizon. Pretend the director has banned every dramatic stick movement.
Plan three shots of one landscape: wide, medium from a safe distance, and a gentle departure. Keep every route clear.
Capture a slow pullback while keeping a distant subject framed. Check the entire route first and retain generous clearance.
Film the same empty scene with two safe camera angles. Decide which hides less useful information.
At a permitted site, record an establishing shot with a slow yaw and a deliberate stationary beginning and ending.
Create a twenty-second landscape sequence that contains no orbit at all. Let the composition do the work.
Practise three smooth starts and stops in open space. Review which clip has the least visible jerk.
Film a broad arc around an unoccupied natural feature from well clear. Keep its apparent size nearly constant.
Shoot a distant horizon with the aircraft stationary, then with a slow lateral move. Compare how foreground depth changes.
Record a safe open-area route that resembles a comma when viewed on a map. Give it an unnecessarily serious film title.
Capture an ordinary field as if it were the opening scene of a very expensive mystery. Use a single slow movement.
Make a match cut from two separate flights over the same clear route. Match framing rather than exact position.
Film a smooth low-to-higher reveal in open space, comfortably within local limits and your normal operating envelope.
At a clear authorised site, practise a gentle S-shaped camera path with no sudden change in yaw rate.
Create a landscape clip that leaves room in the frame for imaginary opening credits. Keep the horizon deliberate.
Use a simulator to rehearse a reveal shot before attempting an easy version in open space. Compare planned and actual framing.
Record one scene with a slow approach, land normally, then film the reverse direction. Cut them into an imaginary arrival and farewell.
Choose a calm day and film three seconds of stillness before and after every movement. Make the editor's life suspiciously pleasant.
five: In a simulator, fly a large diamond with rounded corners. Make every side take roughly the same time.
At a clear open flying site, practise a long shallow bank in each direction. Compare altitude consistency on the DVR.
Plan a broad open-field route with three turns and no obstacles. Fly it once for smoothness, then review before repeating.
In the simulator, follow a wide line without racing the clock. Count unnecessary stick reversals on the replay.
Make a controlled open-area approach to a large landing zone, settle, then land. No heroic last-second correction is required.
At a permitted open site, fly a generous racetrack pattern with long straights. Make both turns feel like the same aircraft.
Review a normal flight's blackbox or DVR for one repeated correction. Rehearse reducing it in the simulator.
Practise a broad heading change in open space while keeping the throttle transition smooth. The imaginary cargo is a bowl of jelly.
Fly a simple outbound-and-return line in a clear authorised field, within visual line of sight. Return with ample battery margin.
In the simulator, repeat an easy turn at three modest speeds. Identify when you start making avoidable corrections.
Plan a normal flight with a deliberate safe landing reserve. Score the planning, route discipline and calm landing rather than distance.
Choose two distant visual reference points in an open field. Fly a gentle line between them without approaching either closely.
Record a wide, flowing S-turn in clear airspace. Aim for continuous motion rather than maximum lean angle.
In the simulator, practise abandoning a poor approach early and setting up again. Successful retreat earns full points.
Make one calm takeoff and a short familiar circuit at a clear site. Land without adding an unplanned extra lap.
Fly broad left and right turns at a comfortable height in open space. Compare their shape using the DVR, not bravery.
In the simulator, hold a chosen camera horizon through a long gentle arc. Adjust the line before increasing speed.
Draw a safe route as a large question mark over an open field. Fly a simplified rounded version with plenty of clearance.
Review a previous flight and select its smoothest five seconds. Recreate only that easy manoeuvre at a safe open site.
Create a simulator flight that looks cinematic without flips, dives or gaps. Give the resulting clip a wildly overdramatic trailer title.
